title: Stakeholder Journey Deck Templates for Renewals
content:
Purpose and intended use:
This is a lightweight, modular set of QBR slide templates and facilitator notes focused on mapping the stakeholder journey toward renewal. The goal is to give CS teams a repeatable, audience-aware deck that can be assembled quickly for Standard (SMB/Scale) and Enterprise accounts with minimal rework.

High-level approach (what differentiates these templates):
- Stakeholder-first: each deck variant centers on the top 3 decision-makers for the account (executive sponsor, technical owner, procurement/finance) and includes cue cards for each.
- Signal-focused: slides highlight renewal signals and risk indicators instead of burying metrics. Each signal has recommended next actions.
- Ask ladder: progressive asks (adoption, expansion, renewal commitment) with suggested language and timing.
- Playbook snippets: for common renewal scenarios (on-track, late-adopter, at-risk) with runbooks and escalation paths.

Assemble checklist (quick start):
1) Pick variant: Standard vs Enterprise
2) Update account header (owner, renewal date, ARR)
3) Select 3 priority success stories (customer-specific metrics or quotes)
4) Pick 1–2 risk signals and attach remediation actions
5) Final slide: 3 asks and next steps + decision timeline

Deck outline (template blocks) — order can be rearranged depending on meeting length:
- Title & Agenda (1 slide): concise meeting purpose + outcome we want (decision/align/next-steps)
- Executive Snapshot (1 slide): topline ARR impact, renewal window, 30/60/90 adoption bullets (one-liner per stakeholder)
- Health Signals (2 slides): trend sparkline for key metrics + top 3 signals (green/amber/red) with short remediation actions
- Customer Wins (1–2 slides): concrete wins with metrics/quotes, template callouts for what to emphasize to exec vs technical owner
- Product Roadmap Match (1 slide): one-row mapping of customer priorities -> product features (use for Enterprise to show alignment)
- Operational Blockers (1 slide): open tickets, performance incidents, support backlog and committed dates
- Commercial View (1 slide): contract summary, renewal options, typical upsell motion and pricing levers
- Ask Ladder & Decision Timeline (1 slide): recommended asks by stakeholder, conditional asks, proposed decision date and next checkpoints
- Risk & Contingency (1 slide): fallbacks (discounts, pilot extension, dedicated SRE time), escalation owners and SLAs
- Commitments & Next Steps (1 slide): immediately actionable items, owners, deadlines

Slide-by-slide facilitator notes (short cues you can paste into speaker notes):
- Title & Agenda: "Confirm agenda, desired outcome: get yes/align on timeline/identify blockers"
- Executive Snapshot: "Open with ROI statement: 'Since last QBR, we've reduced inference costs X% and improved P95 latency Yms' — pick the headline most likely to resonate"
- Health Signals: "Call out the top fabric: usage delta vs target, latency spikes, error rate. Use color-coded cue: green=continue, amber=watch, red=action now"
- Customer Wins: "Bring a short customer quote (if available). For Enterprise, add a callout: 'This reduces time to insight by Z%'"
- Product Roadmap Match: "Avoid vague roadmap slides — only include features that map to customer asks or that will materially reduce risk"
- Operational Blockers: "Name owners and date commitments; show progress bars for open items"
- Commercial View: "State renewal window and three recommended paths: 1) standard renewal, 2) renewal + expansion, 3) renewal w/ concession"
- Ask Ladder: "Ask 1 (by end of meeting): agree to timeline. Ask 2 (within 30 days): pilot expansion. Ask 3 (negotiation): sign renewal by X date"

Standard vs Enterprise variants — key differences:
- Standard (recommended deck structure): 20–30 minute meeting, 8–10 slides. Emphasis: adoption metrics, quick wins, single commercial ask. Speaker notes are short and action-oriented.
- Enterprise (recommended deck structure): 45–60 minute meeting, 12–16 slides. Emphasis: stakeholder-specific slides (exec/tech/procurement), roadmap alignment, security/compliance callouts, and contract levers. Includes appendix with SLO history and support ticket timeline.

Three renewal scenario playbooks (short runbooks):
1) On Track (renewal likely)
- Signals: usage growth > target, no high-priority incidents, exec engagement active
- Primary ask: standard renewal + expansion pilot
- Actions: schedule commercial call within 14 days, present expanded use case, draft contract amendment
- Escalation: AE for pricing, CSM for usage brief

2) Late Adopter (engagement present but uptake lagging)
- Signals: usage flat, 1–2 technical blockers, low exec meetings
- Primary ask: commitment to 90-day adoption plan
- Actions: propose technical deep-dive, offer enablement hours, set weekly check-ins, tie success criteria to expansion
- Escalation: Solutions engineer joins weekly; CS manager runs OKR cadence

3) At Risk (renewal doubtful)
- Signals: declining usage, recurring incidents, exec churn
- Primary ask: decision on remediation package (discount vs dedicated support)
- Actions: assemble war room, map root causes, propose time-bound remediation plan, present new SLA/credits if needed
- Escalation: Director of CS notified; Sales leadership engaged for commercial concessions

Mini-renewal tracker (paste into appendix slide as pre-formatted text table):
Account | Renewal Date | ARR | Signal | Owner | Next Checkpoint
Acme Co. | 2026-01-15 | $420k | Amber - usage lag | Lina Torres | 2025-10-03
Beta Inc. | 2025-12-01 | $95k | Green - expansion | Ethan Park | 2025-09-20
Gamma LLC | 2026-02-10 | $1.2m | Red - exec churn | Maya Singh | 2025-09-30

Conversation primer (scripts & phrasing):
- Executive: "We're seeing X% improvement in [business metric] that maps to your Q4 goal. What would it take for your team to sign off on renewal now?"
- Technical owner: "We have a short plan to close latency and integration gaps in 30 days — would a joint engineering review next week help?"
- Procurement: "We can propose two commercial options: standard renewal or renewal with a 6-month pilot extension; which structure do you prefer for procurement timelines?"

Appendix content ideas (Enterprise-focused):
- SLO & incident timeline (6–12 months)
- Support ticket heatmap (by category)
- Security/compliance checklist and audit status
- Dedicated enablement plan (names, hours, objectives)

Customizable snippets (copy-paste):
- ROI headline: "Reduced inference cost per 1M tokens by X% — direct savings $Y/month"
- Risk callout: "Open: SRE backlog (3 items), target remediation by MM/DD; current business impact: Z%"
- Ask ladder example: "1) Align on timeline today; 2) Sign MOU to expand pilot in 30 days; 3) Finalize renewal by DD/MM"

Follow-up and playbook hygiene (how to keep this deck useful):
- After every QBR, update the tracker row and slide health signals; archive a one-paragraph meeting note in Confluence (link to CONFLUENCE-1254)
- Maintain one canonical Enterprise appendix per account (SLOs, tickets, roadmap alignments)
- Quarterly review of template language; pull successful phrasing into a shared snippets doc for AEs and CSMs

Open questions / decisions we need from leadership:
- Approve standardized concession ranges per ARR tier (we currently lack firm guardrails)
- Confirm central owner for enterprise appendix maintenance (suggested: Solutions Enablement)

Quick reference: file assets to attach when sharing a deck
- One-page ROI summary (PDF)
- Support ticket export (CSV)
- Product roadmap excerpt (1 slide)
- Contract summary (redlined where relevant)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep slides bite-sized — execs skim; focus on 3 clear asks max
- For Enterprise, prep a 5-minute exec-only summary (slide 1) and a deeper technical appendix to share after the meeting
- Test the executive ROI headline with the AE prior to sending invite

Last edited by Maya Singh — draft ready for CS review.
